Numeric examples in candidate modules are copied, not recalculated: noon 205.870498, SMA200 204.277050, open-to-noon decline 1.4408%, provisional cumulative ratio 1.5470 and recent ratio 1.4381. Parameter/unit/version inventory — Astra correction R1
Primary evidence: the frozen DOSSIER passages located above, plus the original-line-numbered I3 excerpt. This inventory records documented defaults or function defaults, NOT actual settings of the ambiguous screenshot or a deployed consumer. Platform pages have unknown publication date and unknown software version; their retrieval vintages are listed under T1–T6. I3 means source observed at commit 63e877cc4cb6c3e7bd137ac67443cd8bca37cb9b. No new market calculation was performed.

T1 RelativeStrength: security price divided by selected base-security price, a price ratio (dimensionless when quote units match; preserve currency/normalization). Input “correlation with security” selects the base, not a correlation estimator. RS is the ratio plot; SRatio marks its initial level. Specific base, price/session/adjustment choices, sampling and initialization of a saved chart are unknown; the supplied prose gives no numeric lookback to import.

T2 RSI: a 0–100 oscillator of recent gains/losses, not a price ratio. Documented default smoothing is Wilder; overbought/oversold reference levels are 70/30, configurable and not project trading rules. Inputs include length in bars, selected price, averaging type and breakout display. No numeric default length is stated in the supplied platform passage. I3 calculateRSI(closes, period=14) does supply a code default: newest-first closes are reversed, the first period gain/loss changes seed arithmetic averages, then remaining changes receive Wilder recursive smoothing. The length gate is closes.length >= period+1; zero average loss returns 100. The output rounds to two decimals with 70/30 zone labels. Minimum input sufficiency is not proof of convergence or alignment with another provider's warm-up/history. Session, adjustment basis and actual upstream history remain unverified.

T3 APTR: percentage true-range normalization BEFORE smoothing; the supplied documentation describes a “middle value” denominator without complete algebra. Wilder is the default average type, with configurable length and average type. Numeric default length, full denominator implementation, seed/warm-up and saved-case settings are unknown from this excerpt. Do not replace it with ATR/close or invent its omitted formula.

T4 ATR: documented platform default is 14 bars with Wilder smoothing. Units are the input price's units (dollars only for a dollar-quoted series), not percentage points. I3 calculateATR(highs, lows, closes, period=14) instead computes the simple mean of the latest period true ranges; arrays are newest-first before reversal, and each range uses high/low and previous close. The code checks presence of all arrays, highs.length >= period+1 and at least period derived true ranges; the excerpt is not complete upstream validation of equal lengths or finite data. value rounds to four decimals. percent is 100*ATR/closes[0], rounded to two decimals when the latest price is positive (code fallback zero otherwise), a different percentage calculation from T3. Inspected code does not establish live session/adjustment/seed conventions or a valid input merely because it returns a number.

T5 Ichimoku documented defaults: Tenkan midpoint of highest high/lowest low over 9 bars; Kijun analogous midpoint over 26; Span A mean of Tenkan/Kijun; Span B midpoint over 52 bars. Spans are plotted 26 bars forward; Chikou is current close plotted 26 bars backward. Values have input price units, offsets have bar units. tenkan period and kijun period are configurable, with the latter governing additional plots as documented; no undocumented custom-period algebra is inferred. Preserve source-bar time separately from display time and require the relevant full source windows/offset coverage. Full platform initialization/edge handling and saved settings are unspecified. Comparing a historically displayed Chikou point must not import a close unavailable at the historical decision cutoff.

T6 VolumeAvg: volume plus its simple moving average over configurable length bars. Both retain the input volume units; numeric default length and saved-session/warm-up settings are not given. I3 calculateVolumeProfile(volumes, period=20) is a DIFFERENT code study: newest-first current volume divided by the mean of positive historical values in slice(1, period+1). Its input gate is at least period+1 items and at least floor(period/2) positive historical items; zero/negative historical values are excluded. Ratio is dimensionless (rounded to two decimals), avgVolume is rounded to an integer; tier names do not prove institutional participation. It does not establish matched-clock normalization, consolidated coverage or share-unit comparability.

C1 actual saved calculation settings: definitions_version KB-TOOLS-001/marketdata v1; regular-session five-minute price proxies at 2026-10-30 noon America/New_York, UTC−04:00. SMA200 needs exact 200 completed daily closes; five-session change uses the stated exact 205-close union, split-only normalized with no dividend adjustment. Cumulative [09:30,12:00) and recent [11:45,12:00) participation each use 20 fixed prior candidate dates and their separate matching-window mean; this saved case includes 20/20 for each. The ratios are dimensionless and provisional within-feed, not consolidated RVOL. Unknown volume is not zero; whole affected windows may be excluded, with fixed candidate dates and no backfill. Required price/history/split inputs can withhold affected metrics without erasing other valid observations. The bounded calendar/domain and retrospective retrieval limitations in C1 remain unchanged.
